title: Modeling User Engagement Profiles for Detection of Digital Subscription Propensity
label: Integrated benchmark
summary: The paper links a synthetic subscription benchmark derived from KKBOX data. We downloaded 1,000,316 rows and trained a gradient-boosting baseline with chronological selection, separate calibration and final holdout evaluation.
status: Dataset file inspected and source archive checksummed. All local training and evaluation ran successfully. This is an independent scikit-learn baseline, not an exact reproduction of the authors’ training code. The code link documents the estimator used.
implementation: Now connected to the Subscription model page: measured baseline comparison, 80 browsable held-out records and live server-side prediction. The target is a synthetic label, not an observed news-publisher purchase.
fit: Subscription propensity. No randomised offer effect is identified.

title: Dynamic slate recommendation with gated recurrent units and Thompson sampling
label: Company research
summary: A Bayesian recurrent slate recommender with Thompson sampling, evaluated on FINN interactions. Useful for a future content-engagement component, rather than the subscription offer-effect model.
status: Paper and repository verified; upstream implementation not executed. The repository explicitly warns that current data and original code are incompatible; use its v1.0 release for a reproduction.
implementation: Reference only. This application does not implement the GRU or Thompson sampler.
fit: Adjacent: engagement and sequential recommendation, not subscription uplift.

title: Meta-learners for estimating heterogeneous treatment effects using machine learning
label: Core method
summary: A framework for learning how treatment effects vary across readers. Our multi-arm T-learner fits an outcome model per action and differences each against the no-offer baseline.
status: Paper, authors' R package, and EconML Python TLearner source verified. Upstream packages are not installed or claimed to be reproduced.
implementation: Independent, tested NumPy implementation with regularised logistic outcome models. This uses the T-learner framework, not the paper's X-learner.
fit: Direct: who benefits from which subscription offer?

title: Doubly robust policy evaluation and learning
label: Core evaluation
summary: Combines a reward model with inverse propensity weighting to estimate the value of a new policy from logged actions and outcomes.
status: Paper and third-party implementation repository verified; this is not Schibsted or Vend code.
implementation: Independent DR and IPS estimators, with normal intervals from held-out per-reader scores and paired intervals for policy differences.
fit: Direct: does targeting improve contribution compared with a fixed offer?

title: Open Bandit Dataset and Pipeline: Towards realistic and reproducible off-policy evaluation
organisation: ZOZO / academic collaboration · NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks
label: Research codebase
summary: A research framework with a public fashion-commerce bandit dataset and implemented IPS/DR estimators. Strong next step for benchmarking estimator correctness on non-synthetic logged data.
status: Official repository and paper verified. Upstream code and real dataset not run in this application; inspect dependency compatibility before installation.
implementation: Reference only. Our experiment follows the logged-context/action/propensity/reward structure; no OBP package is imported.
fit: Direct evaluation tooling, but its outcomes are commerce clicks rather than news subscriptions.
